protocol.budget_selection: The user requested a budget reaching 24/24 on the existing fixtures. A separate 24-case run at 4096 simulations achieved 24/24 before the timed paired rerun. Budget selection used the evaluation fixtures, so this is not a held-out result. No claim that 4096 is the minimum sufficient budget.
protocol.input_changes: Same rewards, choice names, candidate order, case order and pair order as the original run. Case IDs, graph state IDs and observation IDs were namespaced separately for tuning, pre-run check and measured rerun to avoid identical router-cache inputs.
arms: installed harness-router route_mcts MCP after host reconnect
protocol.native_timing: Date.now immediately before returning a case until Date.now as the first statement in the next functions.exec call submitting the chosen name. Includes delivery, reasoning, response generation, host scheduling and dispatch.
protocol.mcts_timing: Date.now immediately before invoking native route_mcts until its MCP promise resolves. Includes MCP transport, parsing, provider round trip and local search; invocation generation and caller graph preparation are outside the timer.
limitations: Retuned on and repeated the same 24 authored fixtures; not held out or blind.
One existing growing Codex conversation, with prior exposure to the cases; exact active model and reasoning settings not independently captured.
Unequal timing envelopes; no pure reasoning-time or end-to-end task speed claim.
Deterministic chains of three transitions with branching only at the root and zero state heuristics.
One policy evaluation per response does not expose whether an internal Jev request succeeded, fell back, or used cache.
The 4096 and historical 32 results were collected in separate runs with different connection/context conditions, not an interleaved simulation-cost comparison.
